LG Electronics Quarterly Net Profit Jumps, Topping Views
By Kwanwoo Jun
LG Electronics posted stronger-than-expected net profit in the third quarter, supported by resilient performance in its home-appliance, vehicle-component and television businesses.
The consumer-electronics giant, like other South Korean exporters, has faced headwinds from the won's appreciation and elevated raw-material and shipping costs amid conflicts in the Middle East.

Despite these challenges, LG said its established core businesses maintained growth and profitability as it expanded into new areas, including robotics and cooling systems for artificial-intelligence data centers.

The company said Wednesday that net profit climbed 54% from a year earlier to 708.40 billion won, equivalent to $534.1 million, for the three months through September. Compared with the previous quarter, profit fell 9.3%.
The result exceeded market expectations by a wide margin. Analysts had estimated net profit of 463.83 billion won for the quarter, according to a FactSet consensus.
Revenue rose 8.9% to 23.824 trillion won, and operating profit increased 14% to 781.90 billion won, both largely in line with the company's preliminary estimates.
A breakdown of its earnings showed solid third-quarter sales growth in home appliances and premium TVs, but the company warned of continued challenges ahead.

Home-appliance demand is expected to recover only modestly in the fourth quarter, while memory and display-panel costs are likely to remain elevated, LG said. It projected TV demand to weaken as high oil prices and interest rates weigh on consumer sentiment.
Revenue and operating profit at its vehicle-component division were a record for the third quarter, supported by a large order backlog, the company said.
Sales in the segment covering heating, ventilation and air-conditioning products increased as the company continued to expand investments in cooling solutions for AI data centers.
